[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#11-purpose-statement]

### 1.1 Purpose Statement

This standard mandates the use of the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) for all Configuration Item (CI) data updates to the Configuration Management Database (CMDB). The IRE serves as the authoritative gateway ensuring data quality, preventing duplicates, maintaining relationship integrity, and establishing the CMDB as the enterprise single source of truth for configuration data.

The IRE provides the essential mechanisms to match incoming CI data against existing records, resolve conflicts from multiple data sources, enforce data quality rules, and maintain an auditable history of all configuration changes. Without IRE enforcement, the CMDB degrades into an unreliable data repository that teams abandon in favor of shadow spreadsheets and tribal knowledge.
page_texts.6:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#12-scope]

### 1.2 Scope

**In Scope:**

- All automated CI data feeds from discovery tools, cloud platforms, and monitoring systems
- All CI/CD pipeline integrations that create or update infrastructure CIs
- All manual CI imports and bulk data loads
- All third-party integrations writing CI data to the CMDB
- All internal applications and services that create, update, or delete CI records
- All relationship updates between Configuration Items
- All CMDB data synchronization processes

**Out of Scope:**

- Read-only queries against the CMDB
- CMDB reporting and analytics that do not modify CI data
- CMDB platform administration tasks (user management, role configuration)
- Schema modifications to CI classes (governed by separate change process)
page_texts.7:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#13-compliance-level]

### 1.3 Compliance Level

**MANDATORY** - All systems, integrations, and processes that create, update, or delete CI records in the CMDB must route changes through the IRE. No exceptions are permitted for production CMDB updates without formal exception approval through the defined exceptions process.
page_texts.8:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#14-business-rationale]

### 1.4 Business Rationale

The CMDB is the foundational data store supporting critical ITSM processes including incident management, change management, problem management, and service level management. The quality of CMDB data directly impacts the effectiveness of these processes and the organization's ability to deliver reliable IT services.

**Business Impact of Inaccurate CMDB Data:**

| Impact Area | Consequence | Business Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Change Management | Failed impact assessments lead to unexpected outages | 62% of major incidents traced to changes with incomplete analysis |
| Incident Management | Inability to correlate incidents with infrastructure | Mean Time to Repair increases 3x with inaccurate relationships |
| Compliance | Failed audits due to incomplete asset inventory | Regulatory fines and remediation costs |
| Financial Management | Duplicate records cause duplicate purchases | Wasted license and support contract spending |
| Service Management | Cannot map services to supporting infrastructure | Service level agreements cannot be validated |

Enforcing IRE usage ensures every CI update is validated, deduplicated, and properly attributed, maintaining CMDB health as the enterprise single source of truth.

## 2.0 Benefits of IRE for Single Source of Truth

The Identification and Reconciliation Engine delivers critical benefits that transform the CMDB from a passive data repository into an authoritative, trusted source of configuration truth. This section details the specific benefits that justify mandatory IRE usage.
page_texts.11:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#211-duplicate-prevention-and-elimination]

#### 2.1.1 Duplicate Prevention and Elimination

The IRE applies sophisticated identification rules to match incoming CI data against existing records, preventing the creation of duplicate CIs that corrupt data quality:

| Benefit | Description | Measurable Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Key Matching | Matches CIs using authoritative identifiers such as serial numbers and instance IDs | 99%+ accurate identification |
| Secondary Key Fallback | Uses alternative attributes when primary keys are unavailable | Reduces unmatched records by 80% |
| Fuzzy Matching | Identifies potential duplicates with similar but not exact attributes | Flags duplicates for manual review |
| Duplicate Merge Workflow | Provides controlled process to merge confirmed duplicates | Reduces duplicate CI rate to less than 2% |

**Without IRE:** Duplicate rates typically reach 15-30%, with the same physical server appearing 2-5 times in the CMDB under different names or identifiers.

**With IRE:** Duplicate rates maintained below 2% through automated identification and controlled merge processes.
page_texts.12:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#212-data-accuracy-through-source-authority]

#### 2.1.2 Data Accuracy Through Source Authority

The IRE enforces the Source Authority Matrix, ensuring each CI attribute is populated by its most authoritative source:

| Attribute Category | Authoritative Source | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hardware Specifications | Discovery Tools | Real-time scanning of actual configuration |
| Financial Information | IT Asset Management | Procurement and contract data |
| Network Configuration | Network Management | Authoritative for IP and connectivity |
| Application Relationships | Application Discovery | Runtime dependency detection |
| Ownership and Cost Center | HR/Financial Systems | Organizational data authority |

**Without IRE:** Conflicting values from different sources create confusion about which data is correct. Teams lose trust in CMDB accuracy.

**With IRE:** Deterministic conflict resolution based on defined authority ensures consistent, accurate attribute values.
page_texts.13:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#213-relationship-integrity]

#### 2.1.3 Relationship Integrity

The IRE validates CI relationships to ensure they accurately represent infrastructure dependencies:

- **Existence Validation**: Confirms referenced CIs exist before creating relationships
- **Type Validation**: Ensures relationship types are valid for the CI classes involved
- **Cardinality Enforcement**: Validates relationship cardinality constraints such as one-to-one and one-to-many
- **Circular Dependency Detection**: Prevents invalid circular relationships
- **Orphan Prevention**: Blocks relationship creation to non-existent CIs

**Without IRE:** Orphaned relationships point to deleted CIs; invalid relationships create misleading dependency maps.

**With IRE:** Relationship integrity maintained, enabling accurate impact analysis and service mapping.

page_texts.17:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#223-automated-discovery-integration]

#### 2.2.3 Automated Discovery Integration

The IRE provides a standardized integration point for all discovery tools:

- **Technology Abstraction**: Single integration pattern regardless of discovery tool vendor
- **Consistent Processing**: All discovery data processed through identical identification rules
- **Automated Reconciliation**: Continuous synchronization without manual intervention
- **Error Isolation**: Failed discovery feeds do not corrupt existing CMDB data

**Without IRE:** Each discovery tool requires custom integration logic; inconsistent approaches lead to data quality issues.

**With IRE:** Standardized integration reduces implementation time by 60% and eliminates tool-specific data quality problems.
page_texts.19:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#231-complete-audit-trail]

#### 2.3.1 Complete Audit Trail

The IRE generates comprehensive audit records for every CI modification:

| Audit Element | Description | Compliance Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Change Timestamp | Precise time of every modification | Supports forensic analysis |
| Source Attribution | Which system initiated the change | Enables source accountability |
| Before/After Values | Complete attribute change history | Supports change investigation |
| Identification Decision | Which rule matched the CI | Explains reconciliation logic |
| User/Service Identity | Who or what initiated the change | Supports access auditing |

**Compliance Impact:** Complete audit trail supports SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and other regulatory requirements for configuration change tracking.
page_texts.20:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#232-enforced-data-governance]

#### 2.3.2 Enforced Data Governance

The IRE provides technical enforcement of data governance policies:

- **Mandatory Source Registration**: All data sources must be registered and approved
- **Attribute Authority Enforcement**: Only authoritative sources can update protected attributes
- **Data Quality Validation**: Incoming data validated against quality rules before commit
- **Access Control Integration**: IRE respects CMDB access control policies

**Without IRE:** Data governance policies are documented but not technically enforced; violations go undetected.

**With IRE:** Governance policies are automatically enforced at the data layer; violations are blocked and logged.
page_texts.21:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#233-compliance-reporting-enablement]

page_texts.28:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#mr-1-all-ci-updates-must-route-through-ire]

#### MR-1: All CI Updates Must Route Through IRE

All Configuration Item create, update, and delete operations MUST be processed through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine. Direct database updates, API calls bypassing IRE, or any other mechanism that circumvents the IRE are strictly prohibited.

**Compliance Evidence**: Integration architecture diagrams showing IRE in the data path; API gateway logs confirming IRE processing.
page_texts.29:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#mr-2-source-system-registration]

#### MR-2: Source System Registration

Every system that feeds CI data to the CMDB MUST be registered in the IRE Source Registry with:

- Unique source identifier
- Authorized CI classes the source may update
- Attribute authority mappings defining which attributes this source may modify
- Data quality SLA commitments
- Technical owner and escalation contacts

**Compliance Evidence**: Source Registry entries with complete metadata; annual attestation from source owners.
page_texts.30:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#mr-3-identification-rules-configuration]

#### MR-3: Identification Rules Configuration

Each CI class MUST have documented identification rules in the IRE specifying:

- Primary identification attributes such as serial number or instance ID
- Secondary identification attributes for fallback matching
- Confidence thresholds for automatic matching versus manual review
- Duplicate detection criteria and actions

**Compliance Evidence**: IRE rule configuration documentation; rule coverage report showing all CI classes have identification rules.
page_texts.31:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#mr-4-source-authority-matrix-compliance]

#### MR-4: Source Authority Matrix Compliance

All CI attribute updates MUST respect the Source Authority Matrix, which defines the authoritative source for each CI class and attribute combination. When multiple sources provide conflicting values, the IRE MUST apply the authority matrix to determine the correct value.

**Compliance Evidence**: Source Authority Matrix documentation; IRE logs showing authority-based conflict resolution.
page_texts.32:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#mr-5-audit-trail-for-all-ci-changes]

#### MR-5: Audit Trail for All CI Changes

Every CI modification processed through IRE MUST generate an audit record including:

- Timestamp of change
- Source system identifier
- Before and after attribute values
- Identification rule applied
- Reconciliation decisions made
- User or service account initiating the change

**Compliance Evidence**: Audit log retention verification; sample audit trail review during compliance assessments.
page_texts.33:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#mr-6-duplicate-prevention-enforcement]

#### MR-6: Duplicate Prevention Enforcement

The IRE MUST prevent creation of duplicate CI records by:

- Applying identification rules before CI creation
- Flagging potential duplicates for review when confidence is below threshold
- Blocking automatic creation when high-confidence duplicate detected
- Providing merge workflow for confirmed duplicates

**Compliance Evidence**: Duplicate detection metrics; monthly duplicate rate reports; merge audit trail.
page_texts.34:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#mr-7-relationship-validation]

#### MR-7: Relationship Validation

CI relationship updates MUST be validated by IRE to ensure:

- Referenced CIs exist in the CMDB
- Relationship types are valid for the CI classes involved
- Circular relationship detection and prevention
- Relationship cardinality constraints are respected

**Compliance Evidence**: Relationship validation logs; orphan relationship reports.
page_texts.36:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#rp-1-event-driven-updates-for-dynamic-infrastructure]

#### RP-1: Event-Driven Updates for Dynamic Infrastructure

Source systems managing dynamic infrastructure such as cloud auto-scaling and container orchestration SHOULD implement event-driven updates through IRE rather than relying solely on scheduled discovery to minimize data staleness.
page_texts.37:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#rp-2-staged-rollout-for-new-integrations]

#### RP-2: Staged Rollout for New Integrations

New source system integrations SHOULD be deployed in stages:

1. Shadow mode where IRE processes but does not commit changes
2. Manual approval mode where all changes require human approval
3. Automatic mode with sampling audit
4. Full automatic mode
page_texts.38:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#rp-3-ci-lifecycle-state-management]

#### RP-3: CI Lifecycle State Management

Source systems SHOULD update CI lifecycle states including planned, deployed, operational, maintenance, and decommissioned through IRE to maintain accurate operational status.
page_texts.39:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#rp-4-batch-processing-windows]

#### RP-4: Batch Processing Windows

High-volume discovery feeds SHOULD schedule bulk processing during off-peak hours to minimize CMDB performance impact, using IRE batch processing capabilities.
page_texts.40:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#rp-5-error-handling-and-retry]

#### RP-5: Error Handling and Retry

Integrations SHOULD implement exponential backoff retry logic when IRE returns transient errors, with dead-letter queuing for persistent failures requiring investigation.
page_texts.42:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#pp-1-direct-cmdb-database-access]

#### PP-1: Direct CMDB Database Access

Direct SQL or database-level access to create, update, or delete CI records is PROHIBITED. All modifications must flow through IRE APIs.

**Rationale**: Bypasses identification rules, breaks audit trail, risks duplicate creation.
page_texts.43:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#pp-2-ire-bypass-for-emergency-updates]

#### PP-2: IRE Bypass for Emergency Updates

Bypassing IRE for urgent CI updates is PROHIBITED. Emergency changes must still route through IRE using expedited processing flags if available.

**Rationale**: Emergency bypasses create data quality debt that accumulates and undermines CMDB reliability.
page_texts.44:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#pp-3-hardcoded-ci-system-ids]

#### PP-3: Hardcoded CI System IDs

Integrations MUST NOT store or reference CMDB internal system IDs. All CI references must use business identifiers processed through IRE identification rules.

**Rationale**: System IDs may change during CMDB migrations or duplicate merges.
page_texts.45:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#pp-4-bulk-delete-without-reconciliation]

#### PP-4: Bulk Delete Without Reconciliation

Mass CI deletion operations MUST NOT be performed without IRE reconciliation to validate deletion candidates against all source systems.

**Rationale**: Premature deletion destroys historical data and breaks relationship integrity.
page_texts.46:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#pp-5-shadow-cmdb-databases]

#### PP-5: Shadow CMDB Databases

Creating parallel CI databases or caches that receive updates outside IRE governance is PROHIBITED.

**Rationale**: Shadow databases become authoritative over time, undermining single source of truth.
page_texts.48:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#exception-request-requirements]

#### Exception Request Requirements

1. **Business Justification**: Documented explanation of why IRE cannot be used
2. **Risk Assessment**: Analysis of data quality risks from bypassing IRE
3. **Mitigation Plan**: Compensating controls to ensure data quality
4. **Duration**: Exceptions must have defined end dates with maximum of 90 days
5. **Remediation Plan**: Steps to achieve compliance before exception expires
page_texts.49:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#approval-authority]

#### Approval Authority

| Exception Type | Duration | Approval Authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Temporary Technical | Up to 30 days | CMDB Administrator |
| Extended Technical | 31-90 days | CMDB Owner plus Architecture Review |
| Permanent | Not applicable | Not permitted - requires standard revision |
page_texts.50:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#exception-monitoring]

#### Exception Monitoring

All approved exceptions must:

- Be logged in the Exception Registry
- Include weekly data quality audits during exception period
- Trigger automatic escalation if data quality degrades
- Be reviewed for extension or closure at 50% duration

---
page_texts.52:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#41-ire-processing-requirements]

### 4.1 IRE Processing Requirements

| Requirement | Specification | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Processing Latency | 5 seconds or less for single CI operations | Support real-time integrations |
| Batch Throughput | 1,000 CIs per minute or greater | Handle discovery scan volumes |
| Availability | 99.9% uptime during business hours | Critical path for CMDB updates |
| Identification Accuracy | 99% or greater correct matches | Prevent duplicates and mismatches |
| Audit Retention | 7 years minimum | Compliance and forensic requirements |
page_texts.54:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#constraint-c-1-single-entry-point]

#### Constraint C-1: Single Entry Point

All CI data must enter CMDB through IRE. No alternative paths are architecturally permitted. The IRE serves as the mandatory gateway between all source systems and the CMDB.
page_texts.55:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#constraint-c-2-synchronous-identification]

#### Constraint C-2: Synchronous Identification

Identification rules must execute synchronously before CI commit to prevent duplicate creation race conditions. Asynchronous identification is not permitted for create operations.
page_texts.56:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#constraint-c-3-transactional-integrity]

#### Constraint C-3: Transactional Integrity

CI updates and their audit records must be committed atomically. Partial commits are not permitted. If audit logging fails, the CI update must also fail.
page_texts.57:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#constraint-c-4-source-isolation]

#### Constraint C-4: Source Isolation

Failures in one source system integration must not impact other integrations or the IRE platform itself. Circuit breakers must isolate failing sources.
page_texts.58:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#43-technology-standards]

### 4.3 Technology Standards

| Component | Approved Technology | Configuration Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IRE Platform | ServiceNow IRE | Must support all identification rule types |
| API Gateway | Enterprise API Gateway | OAuth 2.0 authentication required; see Section 4.5 |
| Message Queue | Apache Kafka, Amazon SQS, or equivalent | For async batch processing |
| Audit Storage | Immutable log storage | WORM compliance for audit retention |
page_texts.60:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#real-time-integration-requirements]

#### Real-Time Integration Requirements

All real-time integrations must implement:

- OAuth 2.0 or mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication per enterprise security standards
- Correlation ID propagation for distributed tracing
- Error handling with exponential backoff retry
- Dead-letter queue for unprocessable messages
- Health check endpoints for monitoring
- TLS 1.2 minimum for all API communications
page_texts.61:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#batch-integration-requirements]

#### Batch Integration Requirements

All batch integrations must implement:

- Pre-validation of batch data before IRE submission
- Chunked processing for large batches with recommended size of 500 CIs per chunk
- Progress tracking and checkpoint restart capability
- Summary reporting of batch processing results
- Rollback capability for failed batches
- Secure file transfer using SFTP or HTTPS
page_texts.62:

All systems integrating with the CMDB must route CI data through the IRE to maintain data quality and single source of truth integrity.

| Integration Type | Examples | IRE Requirement | Recommended Approach |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Scheduled Discovery | Network discovery, VMware scans | MANDATORY | Batch processing via IRE API |

#### Integration Implementation Checklist

- Source system registered in IRE Source Registry
- CI class mappings defined from source to CMDB
- Identification rules configured for affected CI classes
- Source authority established for attributes this integration updates
- Authentication mechanism implemented per Section 4.5 security requirements
- Service account registered per GUID-SEC-IAM-NON-HUMAN-001
- Error handling implemented with retry logic
- Dead-letter queue configured for failed operations
- Logging implemented with correlation IDs
- Shadow mode testing completed successfully
- Security review completed
- Production enablement approved

### 5.2 Bulk Data Import Guidance

Bulk data imports represent high-risk operations requiring additional safeguards. All bulk imports must process through IRE with appropriate controls.

page_texts.70:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#bulk-import-process]

#### Bulk Import Process

1. **Prepare**: Extract and validate source data; transform to canonical format
2. **Stage**: Upload to staging area; run IRE preview in dry run mode
3. **Review**: Analyze preview results; address identification issues
4. **Approve**: Obtain required approval based on import size
5. **Execute**: Run IRE batch import during approved window
6. **Verify**: Validate CI counts; run data quality checks; document results
page_texts.71:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#bulk-import-checklist]

#### Bulk Import Checklist

**Pre-Import:**

- Import request documented with business justification
- Source data extracted and validated
- Data transformed to canonical format
- Duplicate check performed on import dataset
- Dry-run executed and results reviewed
- Approval obtained if required
- Rollback plan documented if more than 100 CIs

**Post-Import:**

- CI count validation completed
- Sample CI verification performed
- Data quality metrics reviewed
- Import results documented
- Lessons learned captured

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#example-1-cloud-discovery-integration]

#### Example 1: Cloud Discovery Integration

**Context:** AWS discovery tool feeding EC2 instance data to CMDB through event-driven integration.

**Implementation Approach:**

- Registered AWS Discovery as source with authority over cloud-specific attributes
- Configured identification rule using instance_id as primary key with 100% confidence
- Implemented event-driven integration using AWS CloudWatch Events
- Set lifecycle rules to auto-retire CIs when instances terminate

**Results:**

- 100% of EC2 CIs processed through IRE identification rules
- Zero duplicates created in 6 months of operation
- CI data latency reduced from 24 hours with batch to less than 5 minutes with event-driven

**Lessons Learned:**

- Cloud instance IDs provide stable unique identification
- Event-driven updates essential for dynamic cloud infrastructure
- Tag-based attributes require clear authority matrix
page_texts.87:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#example-2-legacy-itam-integration]

#### Example 2: Legacy ITAM Integration

**Context:** 15-year-old IT Asset Management system with limited API capabilities requiring batch integration.

**Implementation Approach:**

- Created file-based integration using IRE batch import API
- Implemented nightly export from ITAM for IRE processing
- Configured ITAM as authority for financial attributes including cost center, purchase date, and vendor
- Added data quality rules to reject records with invalid serial numbers

**Results:**

- 98.5% of ITAM records successfully reconciled with CMDB
- Financial attributes now accurate and authoritative
- Data quality issues identified and corrected at source

**Lessons Learned:**

- Legacy systems can achieve compliance with batch-based approach
- Data quality rules catch upstream issues before CMDB pollution
- Clear authority matrix prevents conflicts with discovery tools
page_texts.88:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md#example-3-cicd-pipeline-integration]

#### Example 3: CI/CD Pipeline Integration

**Context:** Jenkins and Terraform deployments automatically registering infrastructure CIs in CMDB.

**Implementation Approach:**

- Registered deployment pipeline as source with authority for environment and application attributes
- Implemented webhook integration from deployment pipeline to IRE API
- Configured identification using Terraform resource IDs and cloud instance IDs
- Created CI relationships linking deployed resources to applications

**Results:**

- Zero manual CI creation for infrastructure deployments
- Application-to-infrastructure relationships 100% accurate
- Change records automatically linked to deployed CIs

**Lessons Learned:**

- Infrastructure as Code provides excellent CI identification through resource IDs
- Pipeline integration eliminates deployment-to-CMDB lag entirely
- Relationship creation should be part of standard deployment pattern
